meta.title: Holiday cottage with spa & sauna in the Vosges (Alsace) – Sleeps up to 10
meta.description: Holiday rental in Storckensohn (Vosges, Alsace): renovated former farmhouse with garden, terrace, spa & sauna. Ideal for nature breaks, hiking, swimming, cycling and skiing.

hero.title: Welcome to the Gîte
hero.intro1: The Gîte Au fil de l'eau offers a peaceful setting to relax in the heart of the High Vosges in Alsace, in the small village of Storckensohn.
hero.intro2: Located in a renovated former farmhouse turned into a comfortable country home, the gîte can accommodate up to 10 guests.

items.kitchen: A fully equipped kitchen opening onto the living room
items.dining: The dining room and the veranda with piano and wood-burning stove
items.tvRoom: A second lounge with TV and DVD player set up in the former barn
items.bedroom: A bedroom with a 140 x 190 cm bed and an en-suite bathroom (walk-in shower, washbasin, toilet)

items.bedrooms: Three bedrooms, each with its own en-suite bathroom (shower or bath, washbasin and WC) and 90 × 200 cm beds that can be combined to form 180 × 200 cm beds
items.mezzanine: A small mezzanine lounge in the former barn

wellness.text: A wellness area with spa, sauna, bathroom and loungers is accessible by lift on level -1. Its large bay windows open onto the orchard meadow along the stream.

baby.title: The following baby equipment is available in the gîte:

items.chairs: 1 traditional high chair and 2 high chairs suitable for different ages
items.bath: A small baby bath and a potty
items.kitchen: A bottle warmer, a baby food maker and unbreakable tableware

accessibility.text: The ground floor and the wellness area on level -1 are accessible to guests with reduced mobility.

meta.title: The living area - Main communal room of the Gîte Au fil de l'eau
meta.description: A 60 m² living area inspired by traditional wooden verandas, with a lounge and piano, a dining room with wood stove, and a fully equipped kitchen opening onto the main space.

hero.title: The living area
hero.highlight: The 60 m² living area evokes traditional wooden verandas, locally called loewa.

livingArea.title: The living area includes:

items.diningWoodStove: a dining room with piano and wood-burning stove
items.veranda: a veranda with a high table in a plant-filled atmosphere

livingArea.note: It opens onto a terrace overlooking the orchard-meadow by the stream.

kitchen.title: The living area opens onto a fully equipped kitchen with:

closing.main: This large living space offers many possibilities for convivial moments together.

smallLounge.title: A separate small lounge,
smallLounge.text: with TV and DVD player, has been arranged in the former barn, whose rustic charm has been preserved.

meta.title: “Cerisier” Room | Gîte Au fil de l'eau in Storckensohn
meta.description: The “Cerisier” room at Gîte Au fil de l'eau, overlooking the orchard, featuring two 90/200 modular beds, two drawer beds, and a spacious bathroom with chromotherapy bathtub - ideal for couples or families.

cerisier.title: The “Cerisier” Room
cerisier.intro: Cherry blossom tones, raspberry and plum colours… this room reflects the orchard that can be admired through a large picture window, while relaxing comfortably in a rocking chair.

room.title: This room includes:

items.mainBeds: Two 90 x 200 cm beds that can be converted into a 180 x200 cm bed
items.drawerBeds: Two low daybeds, convertible into two 80 x 200 cm single beds
items.bathroom: Private en-suite bathroom with chromotherapy bathtub, double washbasin, WC and changing table

room.note1: Ideal for a romantic stay for two, the room’s generous size also makes it well suited for parents with a baby or for a group of four guests.
room.note2: The bright, white bathroom features furniture inspired by fruit trees, as well as a chromotherapy bathtub for relaxing in a bath of changing colours.

meta.title: “Grange” Room | Gîte Au fil de l'eau in Storckensohn
meta.description: The “Grange” room of the Gîte Au fil de l'eau preserves the spirit of the old barn: wood atmosphere, hayloft window overlooking the orchard, vintage sleds and schnaps bottles, mezzanine lounge, and private bathroom.

grange.title: The “Grange” Room
grange.intro: Formerly used to store hay and farm equipment, this room has preserved the warm wooden atmosphere of the old barn, along with the hayloft opening onto the orchard and its collection of vintage sledges and schnaps bottles, rich with memories.

room.title: This room includes:

items.mainBeds: Two 90 x 200 cm beds that can be combined into one 180 x 200 cm bed
items.bathroom: An private en-suite shower room with shower, washbasin and WC

room.note1: The Grange feels like a journey through time, steeped in authenticity and memories.
room.note2: A peaceful space for quiet reflection, surrounded by objects from here and elsewhere.

meta.title: “Aurores” Room | Gîte Au fil de l'eau in Storckensohn
meta.description: The “Aurores” room of the Gîte Au fil de l'eau faces east, offering morning sunlight, two 90/200 beds convertible into a 180/200 bed, and a bright private bathroom with lively seaside-inspired tiles.

aurores.title: The “Aurores” Room
aurores.intro1: Facing east, this room is bathed in morning sunlight from dawn, revealing a shimmering palette of vibrant colours: lime green, mandarin, tawny and turquoise, ...
aurores.intro2: The adjoining en-suite shower room reflects the same lively spirit, with its multicoloured tiled floor featuring fish, starfish, crabs and turtles.

room.title: This room includes:

items.mainBeds: Two 90 x 200 cm beds that can be combined into one 180 x 200 cm bed
items.bathroom: A private en-suite shower room with shower, washbasin and WC

room.note: Somewhere between alcove, garden and seaside, this room brings humour and energy from the moment you wake up!

meta.title: “Jardin des Senteurs” Room | Gîte Au fil de l'eau
meta.description: The “Jardin des Senteurs” room, located at ground level and accessible to people with reduced mobility, features a 140/190 bed and a private bathroom opening onto the gîte’s edible garden.

senteurs.intro: Its windows open onto a small, tree-filled garden, where wild strawberries, aromatic herbs and edible flowers flourish in the shade of old trees. The woodland photographs decorating the room evoke the gentle poetry of the forest landscapes surrounding the gîte.

items.mainBed: Room with one 140 x 190 cm bed
items.bathroom: A private en-suite shower room with walk-in shower, washbasin and WC

senteurs.note: Located on the ground floor with step-free access, this room is suitable for guests with reduced mobility.

meta.title: Wesserling Park, remarkable gardens & textile heritage – Near Storckensohn
meta.description: Wesserling Park, an iconic Alsace site: remarkable gardens, textile heritage, exhibitions and cultural events, just minutes from Gîte Au fil de l’eau.

wesserling.title: Parc de Wesserling
wesserling.intro1: Set on land steeped in textile heritage, the Parc de Wesserling retraces the remarkable industrial history of this former Royal Manufactory.
wesserling.intro2: It captivates visitors with its five magnificent gardens, officially listed as “Remarkable Gardens”, and with its collection, unique in France, of buildings linked to the textile industry (factories, workshops, the owners’ château, grand houses, industrial wasteland and a farmhouse).
wesserling.intro3: Original and distinctive, the Textile Ecomuseum and the Great Boiler House bring the site’s history into dialogue with contemporary art through lively, participatory exhibitions, as well as striking sound and light installations.
wesserling.intro4: The textile trades are also brought back to life through theatrical guided tours and demonstrations of spinning, weaving and block printing. Throughout the year, the park comes alive with a wide range of garden-themed, textile, cultural and artistic events.

meta.title: Storckensohn Oil Mill | Gîte Au fil de l'eau
meta.description: Discover the Storckensohn Oil Mill, a restored historic site where you can observe traditional oil and cider production techniques, all in an authentic setting in the heart of the High Vosges of Alsace.

mill.title: Moulin à Huile de Storckensohn
mill.p1: Built in 1732, the mill remained in operation until 1962. Apples and pears were used to produce traditional farmhouse cider, while walnuts, rapeseed and sunflowers were brought in large quantities to extract a fine, flavoursome oil. In time, the wheel, inactive and worn, finally came to rest.
mill.p2: The restoration of the mill began in 1991, led by a group of dedicated volunteers. Water from the Dorfbach, flowing proudly down from the Gazon Vert, once again powers the bucket wheel, patiently rebuilt to match the original. The cider press, carved from a single oak trunk over two centuries ago, now produces once more a high-quality juice much appreciated by all: apple must.
mill.p3: What a moment when everything springs back to life. The massive millstone turns again, crushing apples, walnuts and hazelnuts. Old wooden gears and shafts happily transmit the energy throughout the mechanism. Walnuts and hazelnuts soften in the restored oven before making their way to the imposing oil press, once again capable of generating immense pressure. This ancestral machinery, mysterious and captivating, seemingly drawn from the depths of time, still occasionally resumes its work in season, pressing rapeseed and sunflower seeds.

meta.title: Lake Kruth-Wildenstein (Vosges, Alsace) – Nature & activities near the cottage
meta.description: Lake Kruth-Wildenstein in the Vosges Mountains, Alsace: walking, swimming, cycling, canoeing and nature relaxation, close to Gîte Au fil de l’eau.

lake.title: Lake Kruth-Wildenstein
lake.p1: Lake Kruth-Wildenstein is an invitation to relax and escape. With a surface area of 81 hectares, this reservoir is the largest on the Alsacian side of the Vosges Mountains.
lake.p2: The lake is a reservoir with a capacity of 12 million cubic metres, built at the bottom of the Thur Valley between the villages of Kruth and Wildenstein. The upper Thur catchment area is largely made up of rounded Vosges peaks that are heavily snow-covered each winter. As early as the 19th century, sometimes catastrophic spring floods led to the idea of building a dam to regulate water levels.
lake.p3: Construction was finally approved in 1954, seven years after the last devastating flood. Built between 1959 and 1963, the dam was brought into service in 1964. Due to the low flow of the Thur at this location, it was not considered economically viable to install a hydroelectric power station. Today, landscaped walking and discovery areas allow visitors to enjoy the lake and its peaceful surroundings.
